clue.text: There are bargains about, darling-odds and ends

indicators.note: the bargains word goes round the other piece, as 'about' means surrounding

parts.note: snips are bargains, things bought cheap
a pet is a darling, a favourite

explanation.surface: Someone notes that cheap deals are around, darling, just bits and pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There are' only links the wordplay to the definition, and 'about' means surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: Snippets are small scraps or fragments, the leftover bits of anything.

parts.note: a stunning woman, with shatteringly hinting at one who breaks things

explanation.walkthrough: Slang for a knockout beauty is also literally one who breaks things.
explanation.definitionFit: A smasher is British slang for a very attractive person, and literally a breaker of things.

clue.text: There's no answer to such a clue!

definitions.text: There's no answer to such a clue!

parts.words: There's no answer to such a clue!
parts.note: a problem with no solution, a word also used of a substance that will not dissolve

explanation.definitionFit: Something that cannot be solved, like a riddle without a solution.

definitions.meaning: the composer Arthur Honegger wrote the orchestral piece ... 231, named after a locomotive; the waters are the ocean

explanation.definitionFit: The word means peace-loving, and names the largest ocean, which Honegger's piece Pacific 231 numbers.

clue.text: Suppliers of drink to the Navy in America

parts.note: tea is a drink

indicators.note: in says the navy's letters sit within the country's abbreviation

parts.note: US is America
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Who supplies the beverages served to sailors stationed in the States?
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' and 'to the' are link words; 'in' works as a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Large vessels with taps that dispense a hot beverage serve as providers of it.

parts.note: MO is Medical Officer, a doctor
a dish is slang for an attractive person

explanation.surface: A stylish physician has a date with a pretty woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Something modish follows the current mode, so it is in vogue.

parts.note: read the name the other way: mad as an anagram indicator on the following word, whose letters rearranged give threat

explanation.surface: Someone asks which Lewis Carroll figure would hint at menace.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the character's name works as a clue, with 'mad' signalling an anagram of HATTER, whose answer is THREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The tea-party host in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland is a Lewis Carroll creation.

clue.text: The lady turns out to be mortal

indicators.note: turns out says the words are turned into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A woman is revealed as merely human.
explanation.definitionFit: Deathly means fatal or deathlike, as mortal does in 'a mortal blow'.

clue.text: Cox makes neat point, right at the end

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle; a steer is a young ox
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A coxswain makes a tidy argument, getting it right in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like tidy but is cattle (as in neatsfoot oil); 'at the end' just says R comes last. A cox steers a rowing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cox is the crew member who steers a racing boat.

parts.note: an associate is a member of a society

explanation.surface: A clubman is connected with somebody's daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Things associated are joined or connected with each other.

parts.note: a den is a private room for work, a study

explanation.surface: An academic report on the Persian Gulf region.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gulf of Aden lies between Yemen and Somalia, so the port's name stands for the gulf.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gulf of Aden takes its name from the port city at its northern shore.

clue.text: He will somehow refloat her at top speed

parts.note: contracted, he will becomes he'll

indicators.note: somehow says these words come out in some other arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A man promises to get a stranded ship floating again as fast as he can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges REFLOAT alone into FORLEAT; 'He will' contracts to he'll with the apostrophe dropped, and 'her' stays as written at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means recklessly fast, at full gallop.

parts.note: a sapper is a soldier in the Royal Engineers, RE
a beck is a northern English word for a brook; the 's gives the S

explanation.surface: A military engineer named Brook owns some antique violins.
explanation.walkthrough: Brook looks like a surname; it is a stream, a beck.
explanation.definitionFit: The rebec was a medieval bowed string instrument, an ancestor of the violin.

indicators.note: heard says the phrase is to be said aloud for a word of the same sound

parts.note: a wake is a gathering held for the dead, and kitty is a cat

explanation.surface: A bird was overheard rejoicing that the cat had died.
explanation.walkthrough: A wake is a vigil or party after a death, so a pet cat's would be a kitty wake.
explanation.definitionFit: The kittiwake is a small gull of the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Top performers include the old ones with lasting quality

indicators.note: include means the performers' word takes the other piece within it

parts.note: stars are the top performers
ye is an old form of the, as in ye olde

explanation.surface: Leading players, even veterans, are noted for their endurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the old' gives YE because of mock-antique signs such as Ye Olde Tea Shoppe.
explanation.definitionFit: Stayers are horses or people with stamina, who keep going over a long distance.

parts.note: to egg on is to urge

indicators.note: perhaps marks one possible rearrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: Someone presses the virtues of hourglasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Small hourglasses filled with sand are used to time the boiling of breakfast eggs.

definitions.meaning: to give credit to a claim is to believe it
the names listed at the end of a film are its acknowledgements roll

explanation.definitionFit: To credit is to trust or accept as true; credits are also the listed names shown at a film's close.

clue.text: The rest live outside Uganda's capital

indicators.note: outside means the living word wraps round the letter

parts.note: to reside is to live somewhere

indicators.note: capital here means the first letter of the country's name

explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts RESIDE round U, the first letter given by 'Uganda's capital' (not Kampala).
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what remains, the remainder left over.

definitions.meaning: ... vile is a stock phrase for harsh imprisonment, so the word is what vile describes
a tributary of the Rhone in south-east France

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition works only through the set phrase 'durance vile', meaning cruel confinement.
explanation.definitionFit: Durance means imprisonment, famously 'durance vile', and is also an Alpine tributary of the Rhone flowing through Provence.

clue.text: To father anything appears full of danger

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
aught is an old word for anything

explanation.surface: Anything to do with Dad seems risky.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation fraught with peril is laden with it, hence tense and hazardous.

parts.note: stuff is both cloth and bombastic talk; the word names a coarse twilled fabric and pompous language

explanation.definitionFit: Fustian is a heavy cotton cloth and, by extension, inflated or bombastic writing.

parts.note: AB is an able seaman
alone means only, solely

explanation.definitionFit: The abalone is an edible sea snail with an ear-shaped shell lined with mother-of-pearl.

parts.note: X, said as ex, is the Roman numeral ten
worker ants are the classic crossword workers

explanation.surface: Former employees are said to have well-paid jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ex' looks like former, but stands for the letter X, the Roman ten; 'say' flags that example.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenants occupy property and pay rent for it.

definitions.meaning: a station manned by the armed services
MT is motor transport, so a place selling fuel and repairs to vehicles

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally it is a base of the services; in everyday use it is a roadside garage selling petrol to motorists.

definitions.meaning: the chief deity of Norse mythology
read as ..., zero noise, which is silence

explanation.definitionFit: The Norse chief god bears this name; split as nought plus din it means no noise at all.

clue.text: Australian may be against ill-written dope article

parts.note: anti means against

indicators.note: badly written letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An Aussie might oppose a badly drafted piece about drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Antipodes are Australia and New Zealand, at the opposite side of the globe from Britain.

definitions.text: That unhoped That men call age

parts.words: That unhoped That men call age
parts.note: a quotation from Rupert Brooke with a word missing after unhoped; the solver supplies the lost noun, meaning calm

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank: Brooke's line reads 'That unhoped ——, That men call age', and the blank is a noun for tranquillity.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a noun, the word means a calm, untroubled expanse or state of peace.

definitions.note: it is infuriating means it angers, a verb in the third person

parts.note: incense is the fragrant smoke burned in church

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims holy smoke at their son's maddening behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: To incense someone is to enrage them, so something that does so angers.
